newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes lower as NYMEX losses pressure.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes lower as NYMEX losses pressure.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed lower on Tuesday after sharp falls in the NYMEX energy complex dragged London prices lower, brokers said.
June IPE gas oil settled $5.75 lower at $172.00 a tonne, while July IPE was 74 cents off at $19.26 a barrel at 1706 GMT.
Brokers said both markets were playing copycat with their NYMEX counterparts and gasoline which registered strong losses at the open of the New York market.
NYMEX July crude was 75 cents lower at $20.88, June heating oil was 1.77 cents off at 55.75 a gallon and June gasoline 1.77 cents lower at 65.15 cents.
Many brokers saw gasoline's recent lacklustre performance in what should be its strongest period of the year as weighing on the market on both sides of the Atlantic.

They said the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly U.S. oil stock data due out on Wednesday would be the next point of focus for the market, giving further clues about the state of play with regards to the gasoline season.

Brokers said that crude had also been capped by its own gains. The recent rise in crude has not been matched by products prices making for lousy refining margins which have resulted in refinery crude run cuts.

So far BP and Texaco have admitted cutting runs at their joint Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam, and Shell at their Pernis refinery due to poor margins, while other refiners continued to monitor the situation.
